acceptance: Clean macOS and Windows VMs pass without bypass warnings.
verifiedBy: node --test tests/platform/acceptance/windows-installed-acceptance.test.mjs (14/14 pass); node --test tests/platform/acceptance/macos-installed-acceptance.test.mjs (9/9 pass) -- both executed, see commands.log.
observed: This task adds the fail-closed binding gate between the shared orthic.membrane.platform-acceptance.v1 receipt (scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs, the schema the book gate's `node scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs --all` manifest command validates) and the deeper, platform-specific proof MBR-901/MBR-902 already built but left unconnected to that schema: on Windows, scripts/release/windows/contract.mjs's per-inner-PE signtool proof (a SEPARATE schema, windows-installer-receipt.v1, that verify-platform-artifacts.mjs never touches); on macOS, RightKit's real sealed release-manifest.json and the macOS release receipt's recorded hashes. scripts/release/acceptance/windows-installed-acceptance.mjs and scripts/release/acceptance/macos-installed-acceptance.mjs each require both documents, cross-bound by commit/artifact-name/artifact-sha256/version, before returning { status: 'accepted' }; either throws a specific FAIL-CLOSED (or the underlying validator's own) error otherwise. The confirmed defect docs/release/windows.md records -- RightKit signs targets.win.sign.files strictly after NSIS has already embedded the main binary and externalBin sidecars, so an outer-installer-signed receipt proves nothing about the payloads inside it -- is directly exercised by the test 'FAILS CLOSED when the outer installer is signed but one inner-PE payload was never verified (the confirmed RightKit NSIS gap)': a fully schema-valid outer platform-acceptance receipt (trust.authenticode: pass) is paired with a lifecycle receipt where one sidecar's signtool verify is 'fail', and the combined gate rejects it. A second test proves the same for a payload missing from the receipt entirely, and a third proves it for fewer proven payloads than Tauri's bundle.externalBin + 1 requires. Every negative case fails closed with a specific error naming exactly what is missing or mismatched -- never an 'unknown, assume pass' result -- including: a missing lifecycle/macOS receipt; source-ready mode presented as installed acceptance; bypassWarnings: true; incomplete platform trust; a tampered sealed installer on disk; a receipt whose recorded hash does not match the actual .app/.dmg bytes; and an artifact-identity mismatch between the outer receipt and the platform-specific sealed manifest (guarding against a valid outer receipt being paired with an unrelated inner proof). Neither script re-implements signing, notarization, or install/update/uninstall exercising: both import and reuse (never fork) the exact validators MBR-901/MBR-902 already built and unit-tested, plus, for macOS, a real subprocess call to release-macos.mjs's existing verify-receipt command (pure hash comparison, no signing tool).
gap: Real acceptance requires a real `pnpm release:build:mac` / `pnpm release:build:win` run on machines holding the Developer ID / Azure Artifact Signing credentials, producing real sealed artifacts and real signtool /pa /tw + install/startup/update/uninstall lifecycle receipts on clean macOS and Windows VMs, then running `node scripts/release/acceptance/macos-installed-acceptance.mjs` and `node scripts/release/acceptance/windows-installed-acceptance.mjs` against that real output. None of that ran here: this task's hard rules forbid running cargo, pnpm, Tauri, right-release, codesign, notarytool, spctl, hdiutil, xcrun, stapler, signtool, or AzureSignTool from this environment. This task's own test suite (23/23 passing) proves the acceptance logic itself is fail-closed and correctly rejects the confirmed Windows inner-PE gap using synthetic-but-structurally-real fixtures; it does not and cannot substitute for a credentialled clean-VM run.
